Make an Element Navigate to a Page and Scroll to a Section

Source: R/crukNavLink.R
crukNavLink.Rd

Makes one or more elements (typically crukValueBoxes) clickable. A click selects a page in a navbar or tabset, then scrolls to a div on that page once it is visible, and closes any navbar dropdown menu left open by the navigation. Call crukNavLinkSetup once in the UI first.

Usage

crukNavLink(
  valueBoxId,
  navId,
  targetPage,
  targetDiv = NULL,
  session = NULL,
  timeoutMs = 5000,
  asis = FALSE
)

Arguments

valueBoxId

Character vector. Id(s) of the element(s) to make clickable, i.e. the id passed to crukValueBox(). Inside a module, give the id as written in the module (the same string you wrapped in ns() in the UI); shinyjs adds the module namespace.

navId

Character string. The id of the navbar or tabset that contains targetPage, for example the id of bslib::page_navbar(). Not namespaced.

targetPage

Character vector. The value of the bslib::nav_panel() to open. Recycled to the length of valueBoxId.

targetDiv

Character vector or NULL. The full DOM id of the div to scroll to, including any module namespace (for example if module id is "ScreeningModule" and the div id is "BowelScreening", then pass "ScreeningModule-BowelScreening). Recycled to the length of valueBoxId. If NULL (the default) the page is opened without scrolling.

session

The Shiny session that owns navId. Default is NULL, which uses the root session of the app. Only supply this if navId lives inside a module.

timeoutMs

Numeric. How long, in milliseconds, the browser keeps waiting for targetDiv to become visible before giving up. Default is 5000.

asis

Logical. If TRUE, valueBoxId is used exactly as given instead of being namespaced inside a module. Default is FALSE.

Value

Invisibly, a tibble with one row per link registered.

Details

Built on onclick and nav_select. Call it from the server function (or module server) that owns the clickable elements.

Setup

Requires crukNavLinkSetup() in the UI, which loads shinyjs and the scroll helper. Without it the navigation still happens, but nothing scrolls and the browser console reports that scrollToDivWhenReady is not defined.

Things to watch

  • Calling crukNavLink() more than once for the same valueBoxId replaces the earlier link rather than adding to it (shinyjs onclick(add = FALSE) behaviour), so the last call wins.

  • targetDiv must be the id as it appears in the page. Use the namespaced id for divs created inside modules.

  • If targetDiv never becomes visible (wrong id, wrong page), a warning is written to the browser console after timeoutMs.

See also

crukValueBox, crukNavLinkSetup, onclick, nav_select

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(shinyCRUK)

ui <- page_navbar(
  id = "main_navbar",
  header = tagList(
    tags$head(crukTheme()),
    crukNavLinkSetup()
  ),
  nav_panel(
    title = "Overview",
    crukValueBox(id = "bowel_box", title = "Bowel screening", value = "70%")
  ),
  nav_panel(
    title = "Screening",
    value = "screening_page",
    div(style = "height: 1500px;", "Some other content"),
    div(id = "bowel_section", h2("Bowel screening"))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  crukNavLink(
    valueBoxId = "bowel_box",
    navId = "main_navbar",
    targetPage = "screening_page",
    targetDiv = "bowel_section"
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

# Inside a module: several boxes at once, each with its own target
# (module server code)
crukNavLink(
  valueBoxId = c("BowelScreening_Eng", "BreastScreening_Eng"),
  navId = "main_navbar",
  targetPage = "Screening_Eng",
  targetDiv = c(
    "screening_Eng-screeningBowelScreening",
    "screening_Eng-screeningBreastScreening"
  )
)
} # }
